  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:3815476183",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "parallelization could degrade rescan performance on non-SSD disks due to random I/O seeking",
      "quote": "Have you benchmarked this on a non-SSD?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied that fast rescan is CPU-bound on filter hashing, and l0rinc confirmed a 3x speedup on HDD",
      "author_replies": ["c:3816289052"],
      "other_replies": ["c:4282211529"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4282211529",
      "status_by_quote": "I have measured it on an Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700 CPU with 8 cores, 64Gi RAM and a HDD"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2778932090",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "scanning thread competing for mutexes and tasks could starve workers and slow down rescanning",
      "quote": "All workers already process submit task in its own `WorkThread` just randomly trying to acquire mutex from scanning thread is non sense to me.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author updated implementation so main thread only joins task processing to clear the work queue",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2779171041", "rc:2786847431", "rc:3079604567"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3079604567",
      "status_by_quote": "I have changed the implementation so that the main thread only joins task processing when it needs to clear the work que"
    },
    {
      "id": "r:3787364700",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "improve and separate the scanning code structure into a separate prerequisite PR before adding parallelization",
      "quote": "I think it would be nice to first improve the current scanning code structure, then land the parallelization feature.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author split the refactoring into prerequisite PRs #34667 and #34681",
      "author_replies": ["c:3967677390"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:3967677390",
      "status_by_quote": "I moved the test change into https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34667 and the `ScanForWalletTransactions` refactor"
    },
    {
      "id": "r:3944480721",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "update reproduction steps in the description because the commit hashes have become stale",
      "quote": "The current steps to reproduce in the description are stale because the commit hashes have changed since your force pushes.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author updated the reproduction steps in description",
      "author_replies": ["c:4984137425"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4984137425",
      "status_by_quote": "The results have been updated in the PR description"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2940590925",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "remove redundant conditions from the loop check",
      "quote": "These two conditions in this check seem redundant with the same two conditions in the following for loop.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author fixed redundant conditions",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2953541104"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2953541104",
      "status_by_quote": "Fixed."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2940624378",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "submit tasks in batches using the ThreadPool Submit range overload to reduce lock acquisitions",
      "quote": "There is an overload method of `Submit` that accepts a range of tasks & pushes all of them in the queue within one acquisition of queue lock",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author implemented ranged submission after rebasing",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2953056026", "rc:3079552801"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3079552801",
      "status_by_quote": "Done."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2940686723",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "sharing a global threadpool across wallets could let a rescan controller thread process tasks from another wallet's RPC, distorting latency",
      "quote": "Can't it happen that this controller thread picks up the task of another RPC of another wallet, thereby distorting results (from a RPC latency point of view) of this one?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author moved from a shared threadpool to a dedicated one initialized per scan",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2952982030", "rc:3079577515"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3079577515",
      "status_by_quote": "I have moved away from a shared ThreadPool to one that is initialized before scanning and discarded after."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2940920289",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "simplify current_block_index + 1 expression since it equals completed",
      "quote": "It appears that `current_block_index + 1` is equal to `completed` due to a `int current_block_index = completed - 1;` above.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author simplified the expression",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2953544536"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2953544536",
      "status_by_quote": "Fixed."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4616990708",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "return util::Expected<void, ScanBlockError> instead of introducing a ScanBlockResult enum",
      "quote": "As a small nit, I think there were some discussions about not creating more \"result\" enum types, and start using `Expected`. I think it would be cleaner to have a `ScanBlockError` type and return those if `Unexpected` happens.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4617449543",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "ask whether combining block iteration and filtering is an intended behavior change",
      "quote": "This is in fact a behavior change :)",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4617784393",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "consistently use QueuedBlock instead of a std::pair of block hash and height",
      "quote": "nit: in many places you use `QueuedBlock` and in others you use a pair of `{block_hash, block_height}`. I think you could just use `QueuedBlock` always as it represents the same pair.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4617893493",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "validate -walletpar bounds and prevent int64-to-int overflow from GetIntArg",
      "quote": "Maybe we should just throw here if `m_wallet_par` is negative? I think we should require `-walletpar` to be bigger than `-GetNumCores()` and smaller than `GetNumCores() + 1`. Also `GetIntArg` returns an int64 while `m_wallet_par` is a normal int you can overflow the integers and trick a bit the result.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    }
  ],
